questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A warmer country with beach and great nature. I really appreciated the spanish language aspect. And also to enlarge my university experiences so also academic.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Barcelona is a great city but very busy. Catalonien is an amazing country with great natur sites and great culture and food. 
The university is not well organized, and it is hard to find courses and a lot and long lectures with little content.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Information was easy to find the online platform is very nice but not very up to date for the coming semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a welcome day for the erasmus students that was great and well organized. Nevertheless was the helpof the course choices very little and very confusing!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used Badi, I think we were lucky.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Barcelona is expensive and can be difficult to find housing, but friends off mine were also living in flats shared with other people. I think they found out about it via wg-gesucht or some other platform. But a lot of people got spamed!

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Via mobility online. very simple.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: ORI - international office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I almost changed all my courses which I thought I wanted to choose before my semester started.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it early.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Content was fine but way too long lectures wih attendancy.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Lower level than Copenhagen but I had to memorize a lot od content.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Very different. Lectures were very long ca. 2-3 hours often also in the evening. 
And the exams are very different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Molecular and cellular mechanisms of tumorgenesis (I): Cell transformation, 3 ECTS 

That is a really nice course, well organized and very intresting molecular content about the cell cycle.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The way back, gas was expensive and the costs for the highway while driving back.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food more expensive, coffee way less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not participate in Uni sport or clubs. But I joined a local club for beachvolleyball that was great fun.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Beachvolleyball, La Mercé (incl. Correfoc), Street Parties, watching Football (FCB Women) and in general all the catalan festivities. Going to the cinema is very cheap; 6 euros on wednesday. Vermout.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined a local club for beachvolleyball that was great fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The nature in catalunya is amazing hiking, skiing in andorra, snorkling, beachvolley.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: If my spanish would have been better I think the locals are super open, but without talking the language it is difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Group work in the lectures and talking spanish/catalan.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That catalan are bad at switching to english to include non-catal/spanish speakers to the group.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: All the holidays and their traditions.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The univesity is very chaotic, the city is big but a great experience and Catalunya is amazing!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to learn the basics in spanish or more. That helps a lot!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Beachvolley ad I joined a laboratory for ECTS that was cool as well. Going out for food without paying loads of money and a vibrant city is great.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring out university without overlays and figuing out enough ECTS.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
